transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I guess what really brought me in is just... I've been having a little bit of trouble with my focus lately? It's probably not a huge deal, but my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore. 

I work as a jeweler, and when I'm at the bench, I'll kind of... I don't know, I'll jump from reading a customer email, to noticing a tiny saw mark on a piece, to some random noise outside. And then... well, it's a bit embarrassing to admit, but I'll realize I’ve completely lost track of the whole work order. I'm really trying my best to stay on top of my projects, I promise, it's just getting a little frustrating. Does that... does that make sense for why I'd come in?
Have you noticed this same trouble with focus or getting distracted in other parts of your life, like at home, in conversations, or while driving?

Um... no, not really. I mean, maybe a little bit? But nothing major, I promise. Like, I think I'm doing okay at home. I keep the apartment pretty clean and I remember to pay my bills on time. 

In conversations, sometimes my mind wanders, but I always try to smile and nod so people don't think I'm being rude. I really don't want to upset anyone or make them feel like I'm not listening. And driving is fine! I'm a very careful driver. I hope that's the right answer? I just don't want you to think I'm falling apart everywhere, because I'm really trying hard to keep it all together.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Um... well, I really try to stay upbeat, you know? I don't want to be a burden or sound like I'm just complaining. But... I guess, if I'm being totally honest... these past couple of weeks have been a little hard. 

I've been waking up with this... this really heavy, hollow feeling? It's almost like the shine has just gone out of everything. I'm still going to work every day, I promise! I don't want you to think I'm slacking off. But... well, it's really embarrassing to admit this, but I've actually cried in my truck a few times before going in to open the shop. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible and weak. I'm really trying my best to push past it and do a good job for my customers. Is it... is it okay that I'm feeling that way? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it.
Have you found that things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends, don’t bring you as much pleasure as they used to?

Um... I don't know, I guess I'm still doing okay with most of my hobbies. I really don't want to sound like I'm just giving up on everything. 

I still try to see my friends when they invite me out, and I always make sure to smile and be good company so I don't bring the mood down. I don't want them to worry about me. I mean, maybe I'm a little quieter than usual, or... or maybe it takes a bit more effort to get excited about things? But I'm still participating, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting at home doing nothing. Is it normal to just need a little extra push sometimes?
Has there been a time recently when even the things you usually enjoy, like your work or time with friends, felt completely uninteresting or joyless to you?

Um... no, not completely uninteresting. I mean, I really love my job. Working with the stones and the metals, it's... it's a good trade. I don't want you to think I'm ungrateful for the work I have, especially since the shop relies on me. 

Maybe... maybe I'm just a little tired lately? Like, I still go out with my friends and I still do my work, I just... I might not be, you know, the life of the party right now. But I still care about it all! I really do. I'm not just, like, totally numb to everything. I'm still trying hard to appreciate the good things. That makes sense, right? I'm just having a bit of a slow week, I think.
Have you felt like nothing, not even things you used to enjoy, could really make you happy or feel good lately?

Um... no, no, not at all. I mean, I can still feel happy, definitely. Like, if a customer is really thrilled with a piece I finished for them, that still feels really good, you know? I don't want you to think I'm just this miserable person who can't be cheered up. 

I guess maybe the good feelings just don't stick around quite as long right now? Or maybe they're just a little quieter than they usually are. But I can still smile and laugh and appreciate things. I'm really trying my best to focus on the positive, I promise. I don't want to be a downer. It's totally normal to not feel 100% happy all the time, right? I'm sure I'll bounce back soon.
Have you noticed that your mood has felt low or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Um... I mean, I wouldn't say I'm, like, totally depressed or anything. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I'm still getting up and going to work every day. I'm really trying to push through it. 

But... I guess these past couple weeks, I have been waking up with this... this heavy, sort of hollow feeling? It's kind of like the shine has just gone out of everything, you know? Like a piece of silver that's tarnished and just won't polish up. I... I did actually cry in my truck a few times before opening the shop recently. But I made sure to wipe my face and get it together before anyone saw me! I don't want my customers or my boss to think I can't handle my job. It's just a rough patch, right? Everyone gets a little down sometimes, don't they? I'm sure I'm just overreacting a bit.
Have you noticed that you've been feeling unusually tired or low on energy most days, even when you haven't been doing anything physically or mentally exhausting?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I'm completely exhausted or anything. I mean, I'm still getting all my orders done on time! I'd never let my boss down like that. 

But... I guess I have been feeling a little more worn out than usual? Like, when I'm sitting at the bench, my arms just feel so heavy... almost like lead. And doing simple stuff, like polishing a setting or just carrying a tray of stones from the back, it just... it wipes me out. Even if I've had a full night off, I still feel like I've been working a double shift. 

I don't want to sound lazy, though! I'm really not a lazy person, I promise. It's just taking a little more effort to get through the day right now. That's pretty common when you work with your hands, right? I'm sure it's just physical strain and I just need to stretch more or something.
Have you noticed that activities you usually enjoy, like working with stones or spending time with friends, feel less rewarding or enjoyable than they used to?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I still really like working with the stones. Like, when I get to set a really nice sapphire or something, that still feels great. And hanging out with my friends is still fun, too. 

I mean, I might be a little tired, like I was saying before, but I'm definitely not losing interest in the things I love. I'd hate to be that guy who just stops caring about his work or blows off his buddies, you know? I'm really trying to keep up with everything and stay social so I don't worry anyone. It's good to keep busy and stay connected, isn't it? So, yeah, I definitely still enjoy all that stuff, I promise.
Have you had days where even things you really love, like working with stones or seeing a close friend, just feel completely flat or empty, like they don’t bring you any joy at all?

Um, no, definitely not completely flat. I mean, I wouldn't ever want to sound ungrateful for the things I have in my life, you know? Like I said, I still really love my job and my friends. 

I guess... maybe there are moments where I'm just a little too tired to fully appreciate things right then and there? Like, if a buddy calls to grab a beer, I might not be jumping out of my seat with excitement, but I still go and I still try to be good company. I don't want to be a drag to be around. And with the stones, sometimes I just have to focus really hard on the technical part of the setting rather than how pretty it is, just to get it done right. 

But it's not like I feel empty about it! I'm still trying my best to stay positive and appreciate everything. That's the right attitude to have, isn't it? Just kind of focusing on the good stuff, even if you're a bit worn out? So, no, I wouldn't say things feel completely flat at all.
Have you felt like even the things you normally enjoy, like your work or time with friends, haven’t been able to bring you any pleasure at all, even for a little while?

Um... no, no, not at all. I mean, I really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm just sitting around miserable all the time. I'd hate for you to think I'm not trying. 

I really do still get pleasure out of things! Like, even if I'm having a slow day at the shop, if I finish a piece and it looks good, I still feel... you know, I feel good about it. I'm still proud of my work. And if my friends come over, I'm definitely glad to see them. I smile, I laugh... I'm still me, I promise. 

I just... I don't want you to think I'm ungrateful or that I'm just letting everything go. I'm really working hard to keep a good attitude. It's important to keep trying to find the good in things, right? So, no, I definitely haven't lost all pleasure. I'm still enjoying my life, just... maybe pacing myself a little more right now. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Have there been times recently when even finishing a good piece of work or seeing someone you care about didn’t feel satisfying or meaningful to you at all?

No, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or, you know, not appreciating what I have. Finishing a nice setting or, um, seeing a buddy—that still means a lot to me. I'm not the kind of guy who just stops caring about his work or the people he cares about. 

I guess... maybe sometimes I'm just a little too tired to show how much I appreciate it? But it's not like it doesn't mean anything to me. I still feel good about doing a good job, and I still care about my friends. I'm really trying my best to stay engaged and keep a positive outlook. That's the best way to handle things when you're a bit run down, right? Just keep focusing on what matters? So, yeah, things definitely still feel meaningful to me, I promise.
Have you noticed that almost nothing has been able to give you pleasure lately, even things you used to really enjoy?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say almost nothing! I mean, I really hope I'm not coming across like I'm totally miserable or giving up on everything. That's definitely not me. 

I still find things to enjoy, really. Like I said, I still like my work and hanging out with my friends. Maybe I'm just a little quieter about it right now because I'm a bit worn out, but I'm definitely still trying to have a good time. I think it's important to keep trying to enjoy things, right? Even if you're not at 100 percent? 

I just don't want you to think I'm sitting around feeling sorry for myself. I'm really making an effort to stay positive. So, yeah, I can definitely still find pleasure in things. I'm doing okay with that, I think.
Have you noticed that almost nothing has been able to give you pleasure lately, even things you used to really enjoy?

Um... I'm sorry, did I say something wrong a second ago? I feel like maybe I'm not explaining myself very well, and I really don't want to make your job harder or, you know, seem like I'm not listening. 

But, um, no, honestly, it's really not like that for me. I still get a lot of enjoyment out of my day-to-day stuff. Like I was saying, the metalwork at the shop, hanging out with the guys... I definitely still like all of that. 

Am I... am I supposed to be feeling like I don't? I hope it's okay that I still enjoy things. I just haven't noticed losing interest like that. I'm really trying my best to answer you properly and give you what you need, I promise. Is that... is that what you were asking?
Have you noticed that activities you usually enjoy, like working with stones or spending time with friends, feel less rewarding or enjoyable than they used to?

Oh, gosh... I feel like I might be frustrating you, and I really, really don't want to do that. You're asking about the stones and my friends again, so I must be explaining myself poorly, and I'm so sorry. 

But, um, honestly? No, they don't feel less rewarding to me. Setting a nice stone, getting the metal just right so it catches the light... that still gives me a lot of satisfaction. I mean, I know I've been a little worn out, but I still really value my work and the people I care about. I get a lot out of it. 

I'm trying really hard to keep a good attitude about everything and stay grateful for the good stuff. I hope that's okay? Like, I'm not trying to be difficult or brush off your questions, I promise. I just... I really do still enjoy those things. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you felt like most activities, even ones you used to enjoy, just aren’t worth the effort or don’t feel good anymore?

Oh, man... I am so sorry. I feel like I'm really letting you down here. You keep having to ask me this, so I must be doing a terrible job of explaining myself, and I hate that I'm making your job harder. I really am trying to answer right, I promise. 

But... no, I honestly don't feel like things aren't worth the effort. Going into the shop, getting my hands on the metal, seeing my buddies... it still feels good. It's still completely worth it to me. 

I really hope I'm not coming across as stubborn or like I'm trying to hide something from you. Am I... am I supposed to be feeling like things aren't worth it? I just want to make sure I'm doing this the way you need me to. Are my answers okay?
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like your work or time with friends, even if you still do them?

I... oh gosh. I'm really, really sorry. I feel awful because I know you're trying to figure something out, and I just keep giving you the same answer. I must be completely misunderstanding what you're looking for, and I really don't want to be a difficult patient. I want to be helpful, I swear.

But... I honestly still like doing all that stuff. Even if I'm tired, getting to work on a piece or grab a beer with the guys... it still makes me happy. I don't feel like the pleasure is gone. 

Is there... is there a different way I should be thinking about this? I just feel so bad that we're stuck on this, and I really want to give you the answer you need. Am I doing this wrong?
Have you noticed that you have to push yourself more to get the same satisfaction out of things you used to really enjoy, like your work or time with friends, even if you still do them?

Oh, wow... um... I am so, so sorry. I feel like I'm completely failing this interview, and I really don't want to be wasting your time. You've asked me this in so many different ways now, and I just... I must be missing something really obvious, and I feel terrible about it. I'm trying so hard to give you what you need.

But... no, I don't feel like I have to push myself to enjoy them. When I'm at the bench, working with a stone, it just... it naturally feels good. And hanging out with my friends is still just as easy and fun as it always was. 

I'm really sorry if that's not the answer you're looking for. I know you're trying to help me, and I want to be a good patient. Should I... should I be looking closer at how I feel when I do these things? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. I'm doing okay, right?

Have you noticed that, even when you're doing things you used to really enjoy—like working with stones or spending time with friends—you don’t feel the same level of happiness or satisfaction from them as you used to, even just a little bit?

Doc, I... I actually feel like I'm going to cry, I'm so sorry. I feel like the worst patient in the world right now. You wouldn't keep asking me this if I wasn't supposed to be feeling it, right? I know I must be completely messing up your evaluation. 

I really, really want to give you the answer you're looking for. I mean, maybe sometimes I'm just physically tired at the shop, and I could say it's that? But... the actual happiness I get from it... setting a stone, or just joking around with the guys... it honestly hasn't dropped off. It still feels exactly as good as it always has. 

I'm so sorry to keep saying no. Please don't be frustrated with me. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or block what you're doing. Is it... is it really bad that I don't feel that way? I just want to make sure you're not mad at me for messing this up.

Have you noticed that, even when you're doing things you used to really enjoy — like working with stones or spending time with friends — you don't feel the same level of happiness or satisfaction from them as you used to, even just a little bit?

I... wait, I'm sorry, I think... did you just ask me that? Oh man, I am so sorry, I must be driving you completely crazy. I really wish I could just say yes so you could get the information you need for your notes. I honestly do. 

If... if it helps, I can just say yes? Like, maybe I just haven't noticed it, and you're seeing something I'm not? I'm totally willing to put that down if it's what's supposed to be happening. But from what I can tell on my end, working on the jewelry and seeing my buddies... it really does still make me happy. 

I'm so, so sorry to keep giving you the exact same answer. Am I completely failing this? Please tell me I'm not making your job impossible right now, I really want to do this right.
